result.title: Where to Start, How to Move: Analyzing Curricula under GRPO for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
result.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Minchan Kim and Sungho Bae contributed equally
result.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) provides no reward-relative learning signal when all rollouts receive identical rewards. In long-horizon tasks that require multiple interactions, rewards are given only upon successful task completion, making all-fail groups common early in training and limiting opportunities to practice later steps. Guide Assisted GRPO replays a successful reference prefix before the learner continues. We study how initial positions, handoff units, and movement rules affect unassisted task completion. Across three model sizes on BFCL, starting near completion is more effective under a fixed turn-level threshold rule. Finer handoffs alone do not consistently help, but outcome-informed tool-call selection outperforms GRPO on trained and untrained task categories. Guided starts also improve AppWorld success on both evaluation splits. These findings highlight where learning starts and how starting positions move as key curriculum choices.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究长时程 LLM agent 的 GRPO 训练课程：通过回放成功参考前缀（Guide Assisted GRPO），考察起始位置、交接单元与位置移动规则对无辅助任务完成率的影响，并在 BFCL 与 AppWorld 上跨三个模型规模比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从哪里开始学习、起始位置如何移动」的课程与轨迹前缀回放设计，可能为 LVR 的 latent 轨迹训练、步骤级监督与贡献分配提供可供核查的方法线索；但论文为纯文本 agent RL，未涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理。
